title.narrative: Strengthening Food Systems and Food and Nutrition Security in Beira Corridor, Mozambique (Mangwana)

description.narrative: A consortium of Technoserve, Resilience BV, Agência de Desenvolvimento Econômico da Província de Manica (ADEM) and the Zambeze Valley Development Agency (ZVDA) has partnered with the Embassy for the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN) to support The Embassy’s EUR 30 million investment in the Beira Corridor. The consortium partners will collaborate to strengthen food systems, food and nutrition security. Mangwana, meaning ‘tomorrow’ in the local languages spoken in the Beira Corridors, is a four-year programme that will transform the agricultural sector in the two provinces in the Beira Corridor. Our vision of the programme is to steer a better tomorrow by improving local farming systems which will produce nutritious food for the people of the Beira Corridor, especially women and children. We are investing in the future by supporting farmers to adopt better practices that will improve their food security, incomes and the environment (soil, water and climate). Mangwana will benefit over 227,000 people and contribute significantly to the goals in the Government of the Kingdom of the Netherlands’ Food Security and Nutrition Policy and Framework and our own goals for local food systems transformation.

title.narrative: A.1. Number of people with a more diverse and adequate diet

description.narrative: Dietary diversity, simply stated, refers to the degree of variety in foods that people consume on a regular basis. ‘Adequate’ here indicates that this diversity should consist of foods across different food ‘groups’ (e.g. whole grains, dairy, pulses), and that limited or no foods are consumed that could lead to health risks when eaten in excess (e.g. free sugars, saturated fat, salt, red meats, and ultra-processed foods). This indicator thus refers to the number of people with an increase in diversity in their diet (as measured through appropriate indicators; MAD for Children a and MDD – FOR Woman). As the reporting is for the inception period and the frequency of reporting for this this indicator is Baseline + Endline (+ mid-term if applicable), the achievement regarding the inception period will be zero.

In other words, the intervention in itself cannot be assumed to lead to measurable (long-term) outcome results. Examples: providing access to digital weather forecast for specific farmers; one-time (group) training on land degradation, (…) As we are reporting the inception period, the number of farmers reached will be zero, as we are working on the beneficiary registration process.

title.narrative: B.1.a. Number of small-scale food producers who progressively realize a living income

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of SSFPs who raise their income towards a living income* for their household. The income increase should be at least 10% (see also under Methodology/Calculation). Farm income includes income from crop production, livestock production, fisheries and aquaculture production, and from forestry production. Here, (gross) income is given by the revenues from such production minus the operating costs of production. As the frequency for reporting this indicator is at Endline (+ mid-term if applicable) the achievement of this reporting period will be zero.

title.narrative: B.1.b. Number of small-scale food producers who progressively decrease the yield gap

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of SSFPs who structurally raise their average crop yield towards the potential yield, thus diminishing the yield gap*. The yield increase should be at least 20% (see also under Methodology/Calculation). The yield gap refers to the difference between potential crop yield (Yp) and actual crop yield (Ya) in a certain (climatic) area, which can be expressed in tonnes or kg per hectare (on average per harvest or per year). As the frequency for reporting this indicator is at Endline (+ mid-term if applicable) the achievement for this reporting period will be zero.

title.narrative: C.1. Number of hectares of farmland under at least 2 conservation practices

description.narrative: This indicator thus refers to the amount of farmland (in hectares) that is structurally under at least 2 conservation practices – of which at least 1 is new (i.e. practices that were not or only minimally exercised before). Note: this concerns practices exercised in such a way that they target a measurable improvement of agro-ecological conditions (e.g. soil quality, water infiltration or regenerative capacity). *Including pastures and fishing grounds (e.g. silvopasture can be a conservation practice for livestock farming).As the frequency for reporting this indicator is at Endline (+ midterm if applicable), the achievement for this reporting period will be zero.
